question: Is the gfx1030 / gfx1201 target_hidden divergence attributable to WMMA?
answer: CONFIRMED CONTRIBUTOR, NOT ISOLATED AS SOLE CAUSE

evidence_wmma_is_used.method: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace of the default gfx1201 BF16-series teacher-forced run, one condition
evidence_wmma_is_used.note: all three are 27B target MLP prefill shapes: gate/up K5120 N17408, down K17408 N5120, plus the Kahan lookahead variant

counterpart_on_gfx1030.note: RDNA2 gfx1030 has no matrix cores, so the same MLP prefill matmul necessarily uses a different accumulation scheme

isolation_attempt.method: SLLM_NVFP4_W4A4_FORCE_BASELINE=1 on both targets, compare target_hidden
isolation_attempt.error: Qwen node layer.0.mlp_gate_matmul.qwen38_projection_pack2 failed: backend status 260: matmul kernel launch: invalid configuration argument
isolation_attempt.defect_note: the documented NVFP4 W4A4 baseline rollback path does not support the Qwen3.8 packed projection node; recorded as a separate defect, not fixed here

conclusion: WMMA is confirmed present on gfx1201 and absent by construction on gfx1030 for the same MLP prefill matmuls that produce the hidden state, so it is a real contributor to the divergence. Whether it is the sole cause could not be tested because the only available alignment lever crashes on this model path. Per the user's instruction this line of investigation stops here.
not_claimed: that WMMA explains all 8/8 target_hidden differences
that removing WMMA would make the two GPUs bit-identical
any statement about the MXFP8 top-1 advantage, which the prior clustered test did not support (p=0.0625)
